mainTopic: Childless marriages and the ten-year wait, and whether a חזקה is set by two times or three
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof from ישעיהו that אברהם and שרה were at first unable to have children, and adds that שרה was an אילונית. Next, רב and רב נחמן suggest that the משנה's ten-year wait was meant only for long-lived early generations. רבה rejects this: lifespans were already short in דוד's time, so ten years still applies. The גמרא then explains why only the husband is said to 'not merit' children. It also answers a challenge from רבי אבא בר זבדא, whose refusal to remarry was only an excuse, and this leads to stories about רב הונא's long lectures. Turning to the משנה's 'a second husband, yes; a third, no,' the גמרא finds a מחלוקת between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about whether a חזקה needs two times or three. It works through cases of babies dying after מילה, sisters together making a חזקה, families with illness, and אביי's tragic marriage to a twice-widowed woman. It also gives two reasons a woman's husbands might keep dying: her body (מעין) or her fortune (מזל). Finally, רבא rules that marriage and lashings follow רבי (two times), while וסתות and שור המועד follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (three times). The source for וסתות continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the verse proof about אברהם and שרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a proof from ישעיהו: the words 'hewn' and 'dug' are linked to אברהם and שרה. This hints that their bodies had to be 'opened up' before they could have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...from where you were hewn, and to the hole of the pit from where you were dug.' And it is written: 'Look to אברהם your father and to שרה who bore you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started just before this point. The second פסוק shows that the 'rock' and 'pit' of the first פסוק mean אברהם and שרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק speaks of being 'hewn' from a rock and 'dug' from a pit, which sounds like something being opened. The next פסוק names אברהם and שרה, so the opening refers to them. It shows that at first they were physically unable to have children.

keyTerms.meaning: you were hewn (cut out of stone)
and it is written (introduces another פסוק)

phrases.english: ...from where you were hewn, and to the hole of the pit from where you were dug,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 51:1. The quote began just before this point in the גמרא.

phrases.english: and it is written,
'Look to Abraham your father
and to Sarah who bore you.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 51:2. This next פסוק tells us who the 'rock' and the 'pit' are.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב, הַבִּיטוּ אֶל אַבְרָהָם אֲבִיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that began on the previous part of the daf.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that אברהם and שרה were at first physically unable to have children.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 51:1-2, where 'hewn' and 'dug' are placed next to the names אברהם and שרה.

steps.title: שרה was an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says that שרה אמנו was an אילונית. He learns it from the extra words 'she had no child.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Our mother שרה was an אילונית, as it says, 'And שרי was barren, she had no child.' This means she did not even have a womb.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement adds detail about שרה. She was not only barren; she lacked the body part needed to have a child at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says שרה was barren (עקרה), so the words 'she had no child' look extra. רבה בר אבוה reads the extra words as 'she had not even a בית ולד,' meaning a womb. This makes שרה an אילונית, and her later birth of יצחק a true miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman born without the physical ability to have children
a womb (literally, 'a house for a child')
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Our mother Sarah was an aylonit,
as it is stated: 'And Sarai was barren,
she had no child,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:30

phrases.english: she did not have even a place for a child.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about שרה's physical inability to have children, which builds on step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שרה was an אילונית; she lacked even a womb, as shown by the extra words 'אין לה ולד'.

steps.title: In later generations the wait is two and a half years
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's ten-year wait was meant only for the earlier generations, who lived longer. Today a man waits only two and a half years, the time of three pregnancies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: The ten years were taught only for the earlier generations, whose years were many. But in the later generations, whose years are few, the wait is two and a half years, matching three pregnancies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule of waiting ten years. רב limits that rule to people who lived long lives in earlier times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that how long you wait should match how long people live. Earlier generations had long lives, so ten years was a fair wait. Now that lives are shorter, רב sets the wait at two and a half years, the time of three pregnancies.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only for... (limits an earlier rule)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not arguing with the משנה. He is saying the משנה's ten years were meant only for long-lived generations, and he gives the matching wait for our times.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said
in the name of Rav:
They taught it only with regard to former generations,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה's rule of waiting ten years without children.

phrases.english: whose years were numerous.
But in later generations,
whose years are few —
two and a half years,
corresponding to three pregnancies.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּדוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of שרה and returns to the legal rule of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten-year wait applies only to long-lived earlier generations; in later generations the wait is two and a half years, matching three pregnancies.
steps.whyThisMatters: It raises the main question of this section: does the number in a משנה change when human lifespans change?

steps.title: Another view: three years, matching three times of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting רב נחמן, also agrees the wait is shorter today, but he says three years. Each ראש השנה is a time when barren women may be 'remembered' and given children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב נחמן: Three years, matching three 'rememberings.' As the Master said: On ראש השנה, שרה, רחל, and חנה were remembered.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different shorter wait: three years instead of two and a half. It supports the number with a teaching about ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרה, רחל, and חנה were all 'remembered' with children on ראש השנה. So each ראש השנה is a new chance for a barren woman. Waiting three years gives the couple three such chances before giving up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'rememberings,' when ה׳ grants children to barren women
as the Master said (quotes a known teaching)
the Jewish New Year, a day of judgment

phrases.english: Rabba said in the name of Rav Naḥman:
Three years,
corresponding to three remembrances.
As the Master said:
On Rosh HaShana were remembered
Sarah, Rachel, and Hannah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with step 3 that the wait is shorter today, but gives three years instead of two and a half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In later generations the wait is three years, matching three ראש השנה judgments when barren women may be remembered.

steps.title: רבה rejects the shorter waiting periods
steps.stepSummary: רבה himself says these shorter-wait rules are not accepted. רבי arranged the משנה long after דוד המלך, and lifespans were already short in דוד's time. So the משנה's ten years were written for short-lived generations too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: These rules are not accepted. After all, who arranged the משנה? רבי. And already in the days of דוד the years were shortened, as it is written: 'The days of our years are seventy years.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes away both opinions from steps 3 and 4. He shows that the משנה's ten years were written for people with short lives like ours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 4 assumed that ten years fit only long-lived early generations. But רבי wrote the משנה long after דוד, and תהלים already says that in דוד's time people lived about seventy years. So רבי knew lives were short and still said ten years, which means ten years is the rule even today.

keyTerms.meaning: after all, consider (introduces a logical point)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה concludes that the משנה's ten-year wait still applies. The shorter waits of two and a half or three years are rejected, because רבי wrote the משנה at a time when people already lived short lives.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same רבה who quoted the three-year view in step 4. He was reporting רב נחמן's opinion, and now he gives his own view, which rejects it.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
These principles are not accepted.
phrases.notes: He means both shorter waits: two and a half years and three years.

phrases.english: After all, who arranged the mishna?
Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi),
and already in the days of David the years were diminished,
as it is written:
'The days of our years are seventy years.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לֵיתַנְהוּ לְהָנֵי כְּלָלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects both shorter waiting periods from steps 3 and 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both the two-and-a-half-year view (רב) and the three-year view (רב נחמן).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They assume the ten-year rule was meant only for long-lived generations. But רבי wrote the משנה after lifespans had already become short in דוד's time.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's ten-year wait applies even in later generations.

steps.title: Why blame only the husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says 'perhaps he did not merit' when maybe it was the wife who did not merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the phrase 'perhaps he did not merit to have children from her': maybe it is she who did not merit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of a ברייתא about a couple with no children. Why does it put the 'blame' only on the husband?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא suggests the husband did not merit children with this wife, so he should try with another. But the גמרא points out that the 'not meriting' could just as easily belong to the wife.

keyTerms.meaning: to be 'built', meaning to have a family through children

phrases.english: And this [phrase]: 'Perhaps he did not merit
to be built from her'
but perhaps it is she who did not merit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא אִיהִי דְּלָא זָכְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the length of the waiting period to the wording of the ברייתא about who 'did not merit'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's phrase 'perhaps he did not merit to be built from her'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Childlessness could just as well be the wife's 'fault', so why does the ברייתא speak only of the husband?

steps.title: Only the man is commanded to have children
steps.stepSummary: The wife is not commanded in פריה ורביה, so she is not punished with childlessness.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is not commanded to be fruitful and multiply, so she is not punished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא speaks about the husband because only he carries the מצוה of having children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not merit to have children is treated as a kind of punishment. Since a woman is not obligated in פריה ורביה, she is not punished in this area, so the ברייתא speaks only about him.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the well-known rule that a woman is not obligated in פריה ורביה.

phrases.english: She, since she is not commanded
about being fruitful and multiplying, is not punished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהִי כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מְפַקְּדָא אַפְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording using the rule that only men are commanded in פריה ורביה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either spouse could be the one who 'did not merit'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the husband can be 'punished' with childlessness, since only he is commanded.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר זבדא refused to remarry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule using רבי אבא בר זבדא, who said that if he had merited, he would already have had children with his first wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? The רבנן told רבי אבא בר זבדא to marry a woman and have children, and he answered: if I had merited, I would have had them from my first wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's rule that a childless man must take another wife. It brings a sage who seemed to say there is no point in remarrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא בר זבדא seemed to say that if he did not merit children with his first wife, he won't merit them with another one either. That goes against the משנה, which tells a childless man to marry someone else.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't the Rabbis say
to Rabbi Abba bar Zavda:
Marry a woman and have children,
and he said to them: If I had merited,
I would have had them from the first one.
phrases.notes: He means his first wife: no children with her shows, he says, that he just isn't meant to have them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's rule that a childless man should marry another wife.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that after ten childless years the husband must take another wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A great sage seemed to say that remarrying makes no sense if the first marriage produced no children.

steps.title: It was only an excuse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא was just putting off the רבנן; the real reason was that he had become unable to have children from רב הונא's lectures.
steps.simpleTranslation: There he was only pushing the רבנן off, because רבי אבא בר זבדא had become sterile from רב הונא's lectures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that his words were not a real halachic opinion. They were a polite excuse to hide the true reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remarrying would not help רבי אבא בר זבדא, since he himself could no longer have children. So his case says nothing against the משנה's rule. The usual explanation is that the students held themselves in during רב הונא's very long lectures, and this harmed them.

keyTerms.meaning: he was just pushing them off

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule stands: a childless man should try again with another wife. רבי אבא בר זבדא's words were only an excuse.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם דַּחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵי לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: There, he was just pushing the Rabbis off,
for Rabbi Abba bar Zavda
became sterile from Rav Huna's lecture.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם דַּחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵי לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case: his words were an excuse, not a halachic position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא בר זבדא held that remarrying is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was physically unable to have children, so his refusal teaches nothing against the משנה.

steps.title: Other sages hurt by רב הונא's lectures
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל, רבי חלבו and רב ששת also became sterile from רב הונא's lectures.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל, רבי חלבו and רב ששת each became sterile from רב הונא's lectures.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא mentioned רב הונא's lectures, it adds a list of other sages who were harmed the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the halacha here. It is a side note showing that what happened to רבי אבא בר זבדא happened to many others too.

keyTerms.meaning: a great אמורא, also harmed this way

phrases.aramaic: רַב גִּידֵּל אִיעֲקַר מִפִּרְקֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: Rav Giddel became sterile from Rav Huna's lecture.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אִיעֲקַר מִפִּרְקֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Helbo became sterile from Rav Huna's lecture.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אִיעֲקַר מִפִּרְקֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet became sterile from Rav Huna's lecture.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גִּידֵּל אִיעֲקַר מִפִּרְקֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more examples like רבי אבא בר זבדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several sages were left unable to have children because of רב הונא's lectures.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב is cured
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב got sick from holding himself in; they hung him from the cedar pillar of the study hall, and something green came out of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב was struck by סוסכינתא. They hung him on the cedar pillar of the בית מדרש, and something green like a palm leaf came out of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story of one sage who got the same illness but was cured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows there was a treatment for the harm the others suffered. It sets up his own statement in the next step about why he alone was saved.

keyTerms.meaning: an illness from holding in one's urine

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אֲחַדְתֵּיהּ סוּסְכִּינְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Aha bar Ya'akov was seized by suskhinta,
phrases.notes: This is an illness caused by holding yourself in instead of going to the bathroom.

phrases.english: they hung him on the cedar [pillar] of the study hall
and something like a green palm leaf came out of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אֲחַדְתֵּיהּ סוּסְכִּינְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with one sage who was cured.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא בר יעקב was cured of the illness by being hung up.

steps.title: Only רב אחא בר יעקב was saved
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says sixty elders were harmed by רב הונא's lectures, all except him, because he applied 'wisdom keeps alive the one who has it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: We were sixty elders, and all of them became sterile from רב הונא's lectures except me, because I fulfilled in myself 'wisdom keeps alive the one who has it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב sums up the story: of sixty elders, only he was saved, because he used wisdom to cure himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as being about practical wisdom. Because he knew the cure, his wisdom literally kept him healthy.

keyTerms.meaning: wisdom keeps alive the one who has it

steps.whatToRemember: The whole story explains why רבי אבא בר זבדא did not remarry. It is not a real argument against the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Aha bar Ya'akov said:
We were sixty elders,
and all of them became sterile from Rav Huna's lecture
except for me,
for I fulfilled in myself
'Wisdom keeps alive the one who has it.'
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:12

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: שִׁיתִּין סָבֵי הֲוֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אחא בר יעקב explains why he alone was saved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of sixty elders only רב אחא בר יעקב escaped harm, thanks to wisdom.

steps.title: A second husband yes, a third no
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה ('if he divorced her, she is permitted'), the גמרא learns that a childless woman may marry a second husband but not a third.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he divorced her, she may marry someone else. That means a second husband, yes; a third, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה and draws a short rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows a divorced childless woman to marry a second husband. The גמרא learns from this that after two such marriages with no children, she is assumed unable to have children, so she should not marry a third man for the sake of children.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'שלישי לא' as a new rule invented here. It is the גמרא's reading of the משנה's words 'she is permitted' to a second husband.

phrases.english: If he divorced her, she is permitted, etc.
A second [husband], yes; a third, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּירְשָׁהּ מוּתֶּרֶת וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A childless divorced woman may marry a second husband, but not a third.

steps.title: Who is the author of our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא our משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote our משנה. This is a setup question, and the answer comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 learned that a childless woman may marry a second husband but not a third. That means two events are enough to create a חזקה, so the גמרא wants to know whose view that is.

phrases.english: Our משנה, whose opinion is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which תנא holds the 'two times' rule learned in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a חזקה is set after two times

steps.title: It follows רבי, who sets a חזקה after two times
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי, as shown by a ברייתא about a woman whose sons died from מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי. As a ברייתא teaches: if her first son was circumcised and died, and the second died too, she should not circumcise the third. That is רבי's view. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: she circumcises the third, but not the fourth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows רבי. It supports this with a ברייתא where רבי says two deaths are already enough to stop circumcising the next son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that two times make a חזקה, which fits our משנה (no third husband). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs three times. The case is about danger: once there is a pattern, we do not risk the next baby.

keyTerms.meaning: A set pattern we assume will continue

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the 'two or three times' argument about חזקה applies in many areas: marriage, danger in מילה, and more.

phrases.english: It is רבי.
As a ברייתא teaches:
If she circumcised the first son and he died,
and the second one, and he died,
the third one, she should not circumcise,
these are the words of רבי.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
the third one she should circumcise,
the fourth one she should not circumcise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי, who holds a חזקה is set after two times, as seen in the ברייתא about מילה

steps.title: Another ברייתא has the opinions reversed
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא switches the opinions of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so which version is reliable?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches the opposite! Which of them is the later, more reliable one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another ברייתא switches the two opinions. It asks which version we should trust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the opinions are reversed, then רבי needs three times, and our משנה would follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל instead. The גמרא needs to know which version is correct before saying who the משנה follows.

phrases.english: But isn't the reverse taught in a ברייתא?
Which of them is (the later one)?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, the question is which ברייתא we should rely on.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ברייתא quoted in step 15 has the opinions right
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of the ברייתא correctly reports רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא gives the opposite attributions, so the identification of the משנה with רבי is uncertain

steps.title: The story of four sisters in ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל told only the fourth sister not to circumcise, which suggests he needs three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There was a story with four sisters in ציפורי. The first circumcised her son and he died, the second and he died, the third and he died. The fourth came before רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and he told her: Do not circumcise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real story to prove what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds. He told the fourth sister not to circumcise, after three deaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems to show that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs three times for a חזקה. That fits the first ברייתא (step 15), so the version where רבי needs only two would be the correct one.

keyTerms.meaning: ציפורי, a city in the גליל

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as רבי חייא בר אבא said
that רבי יוחנן said:
There was an incident with four sisters in ציפורי
where the first circumcised her son and he died,
the second, and he died,
the third, and he died,

phrases.aramaic: רְבִיעִית בָּאת לִפְנֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: the fourth came before רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
He said to her: Do not circumcise.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of step 16 with a real story
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs three times, so the first ברייתא is correct
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the four sisters in ציפורי, told by רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Maybe he would have told the third sister too
steps.stepSummary: The story does not prove anything, because the third sister never asked him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe if the third sister had come, he would also have told her not to circumcise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Only the fourth sister asked him, so we do not know what he would have told the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows he forbade it after three deaths, but not that he would have allowed it after two. So he might hold two times is enough, and the proof falls apart.

phrases.english: But maybe if the third had come
he would also have said this to her?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא אִי אָתְיָא שְׁלִישִׁית נָמֵי הֲוָה אָמַר לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story only shows his ruling after three deaths; it says nothing about what he would rule after two

steps.title: Then why tell the story at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the story proves nothing, why did רבי חייא בר אבא bother reporting it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of רבי חייא בר אבא's testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי חייא בר אבא would report this story if it teaches nothing. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story is only told in the name of great רבנן if it teaches something. If it does not show 'three times', it must be teaching something else.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אַסְהָדוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא?
phrases.english: what is the point of רבי חייא בר אבא's testimony?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מַאי אַסְהָדוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of step 18
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the story does not show the number three, the report seems pointless

steps.title: The story teaches that sisters create a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The story teaches that deaths among sisters' children together can set a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it teaches us that sisters create a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story teaches a different lesson: sisters together can create a חזקה, even though each baby had a different mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not how many times are needed, but who counts. Deaths in the children of different sisters join together to make a pattern in the family. So this story does not settle which ברייתא is correct; the גמרא comes back to that question in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי (two times make a חזקה). The story of the sisters does not decide between the two ברייתות, but teaches that sisters join together to make a חזקה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the story proved רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs three times. The גמרא rejected that and used the story for a different lesson.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes an important rule for מילה: deaths among sisters' sons can be a reason not to circumcise, because of danger.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is what it teaches us:
that sisters establish a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דַּאֲחָיוֹת מְחַזְּקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the story a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story was told to show how many deaths רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs
steps.terutzMaskana: The story teaches that sisters together establish a חזקה

steps.title: Do not marry into families with epilepsy or צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רבא builds on the idea that sisters together set a חזקה. He rules that a man should not marry a woman from a family of נכפין or מצורעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since sisters can together set an established pattern, a man should not marry a woman from a family of epileptics or from a family of lepers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the lesson just learned, that sisters' children together can set a חזקה, and applies it to a new area: whom to marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a pattern can be set across different sisters, then a sickness that keeps showing up in a family counts as a real pattern for that family. So marrying into such a family is a risk, because the illness may be passed on.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have said (building on an earlier conclusion)
(Sisters) establish a חזקה, a set pattern

steps.whyThisMatters: This takes the חזקה idea out of the מילה case and turns it into practical guidance about family health and marriage.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now that you have said that sisters establish a presumption,
a man should not marry a woman
not from a family of epileptics
and not from a family of lepers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ אֲחָיוֹת מְחַזְּקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of step 20 (sisters set a חזקה together) to a new practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man should not marry into a family of epileptics or lepers, because a family pattern counts as a חזקה.

steps.title: Only after it happened three times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבא's rule: it applies only when the illness has shown up three times in the family.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only when it has been established three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רבא's rule: one or two cases in a family are not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the view that a חזקה needs three times, not two. So the marriage warning applies only after three family members have had the illness.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two numbers up: the warning starts at the third case, not the second.

phrases.english: And this is only where it was established three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא דְּאִתַּחְזַק תְּלָתָא זִימְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's rule from step 21 to cases established three times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern about marrying into such a family begins only after three cases.

steps.title: What was the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical bottom line: is a חזקה set by two times or by three?
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses and asks how the question ends in practice. This sets up the report that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, two ברייתות reported רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in opposite ways, so it was unclear whether two or three times is needed. Here the גמרא looks for a real case that settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: What came of it? What is the final ruling?

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?
phrases.notes: He means: in the end, is a pattern set by two times or only by three?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הֲוָה עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the unresolved question from step 16 about two times versus three.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical ruling: is a חזקה set by two times or by three?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן told the third sister to circumcise
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reports a case before רבי יוחנן. Two sisters' babies died after מילה, and רבי יוחנן told the third sister to go ahead with her baby's מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: A case came before רבי יוחנן in the shul of מעון on a יום כיפור that fell on שבת. The first sister did מילה and the baby died, the second did and the baby died, and the third came before him. He told her: Go and do the מילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a real case. רבי יוחנן did not treat two deaths as a set pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two times made a חזקה, the third baby would have been at risk, and רבי יוחנן would have stopped the מילה. Since he let it go ahead, his ruling shows that a חזקה needs three times.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the report אביי later relies on. רבא questions its reliability in step 27, and the final ruling for marriage in step 35 follows רבי (two times).

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר:
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל and brought back reports of rulings made there.

phrases.english: An incident occurred before Rabbi Yoḥanan
in the synagogue of Maon
on Yom Kippur that fell on Shabbat,
and the first sister circumcised and the baby died,
the second, and the baby died,
the third came before him.
He said to her: Go and circumcise.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר: עוֹבָדָא הֲוָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23 with a real ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן allowed the third sister's מילה, so two times does not set a חזקה. Three are needed.

steps.title: אביי warns: be sure, this touches a prohibition and a danger
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יצחק בר יוסף to be careful with this report, because it allows something that could be both forbidden and dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Look carefully, because you are permitting something that may be a prohibition and a danger.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the report and wants it checked. If it is wrong, the result is serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two times really were a חזקה, the third baby's מילה would be dangerous. It would then also break שבת and יום כיפור for nothing. So a mistaken report would cause both a sin and a risk to life.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
See that you are permitting a prohibition and a danger.
phrases.notes: The prohibition is doing the מילה on שבת and יום כיפור. The danger is to the baby's life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: חֲזִי דְּקָשָׁרֵית אִיסּוּרָא וְסַכַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how reliable the report in step 24 is.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן permitted the third sister's מילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stakes are very high (a prohibition and a danger), so a report like this cannot be accepted without being sure it is accurate.

steps.title: אביי relied on it, married a twice-widowed woman, and died
steps.stepSummary: אביי relied on the two-times-is-not-enough ruling. He married חומה, whose two earlier husbands had died, and he died too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי relied on this and went and married חומה, the daughter of איסי son of רב יצחק son of רב יהודה. רחבא of פומבדיתא had married her and died, then רב יצחק son of רבה בר בר חנה married her and died, and then אביי married her and died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: אביי acted on the report himself, and the result was tragic. רבא questions this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two husbands dying is only two times, so by רבי יוחנן's ruling it is not yet a חזקה, and אביי felt free to marry her. After he also died, she had now lost husbands three times.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי relied on רב יצחק בר יוסף's report that two times is not yet a חזקה, married a twice-widowed woman, and died. רבא questions this right away (steps 27-28), and in step 35 the הלכה for marriage follows רבי: two deaths already make a חזקה.

phrases.english: Abaye relied on it,
and went and married Ḥuma
the daughter of Isi, son of Rav Yitzḥak
son of Rav Yehuda,
whom Raḥava of Pumbedita had married, and he died;

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה וּשְׁכֵיב,
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rabba bar bar Ḥana, and he died;
and he married her, and he died.
phrases.notes: "He" here is אביי himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְמַךְ עֲלַהּ אַבָּיֵי, וַאֲזַל נַסְבַהּ לְחוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows אביי accepting the report from step 24 despite his warning in step 25, and acting on it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי acted on the report that two times is not a חזקה, married a woman widowed twice, and died. The report is then challenged by רבא, and the final ruling for marriage follows רבי (two times).

steps.title: Would אביי really risk his life on that report?
steps.stepSummary: רבא doubts that אביי would put his own life on the line based on רב יצחק בר יוסף's report, since אביי himself said that rabbi was not fully reliable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Would anyone really risk his own life like this? אביי himself said that אבין is reliable but יצחק סומקא (the Red) is not. אבין goes back to ארץ ישראל and hears when rulings change, but יצחק סומקא does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the story from step 26, where אביי married חומה because he relied on רב יצחק בר יוסף's report. רבא asks how אביי could rely on a source he himself called unreliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר יוסף reported that רבי יוחנן allowed a third מילה after two deaths, meaning two times is not a חזקה. אביי once said this rabbi does not go back to ארץ ישראל, so he might miss it if a ruling was changed. Risking your life on such a report seems unlikely.

keyTerms.meaning: reliable, someone you can depend on

phrases.english: Rava said:
And is there anyone who would do such an act
with his own life, like this?
phrases.notes: He means putting your own life at risk by marrying a woman whose two husbands died.

phrases.english: But wasn't it he who said:
phrases.notes: "He" is אביי.

phrases.english: Avin is reliable,
Yitzchak the Red is not reliable.
phrases.notes: This is רב יצחק בר יוסף, who told the story about רבי יוחנן in step 24.

phrases.english: Avin goes back,
phrases.notes: He goes back to ארץ ישראל, so he would hear if the rabbis there changed a ruling.

phrases.english: Yitzchak the Red does not go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא דְּעָבֵיד עוֹבָדָא בְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ כִּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in step 26 about אביי marrying חומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אביי relied on רב יצחק בר יוסף's report when he married חומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי himself called this rabbi unreliable because he might not hear about changed rulings. It is unlikely that אביי would risk his life on such a source.

steps.title: Maybe the argument is only about circumcision
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a second problem. Even if the opinions argue about two versus three deaths for מילה, who says they argue about marriage?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: maybe they argue only about מילה. Do they really argue about marriage?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second reason the story about אביי is hard to accept. The ruling about מילה might not carry over to marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story in step 24 was about babies dying after מילה. Even if two times is not a חזקה there, marriage could have a different rule. In that case אביי had no basis for his marriage.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
say that they disagree regarding circumcision,
phrases.notes: "They" are the opinions arguing whether a pattern needs two times or three.

phrases.english: do they disagree regarding marriage?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: אֵימַר דִּפְלִיגִי לְעִנְיַן מִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the one in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the מילה ruling to marriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The argument might exist only for מילה. If so, nothing allowed a woman whose two husbands died to marry a third.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows they argue about marriage too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the second challenge. A ברייתא shows that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about a woman whose husbands died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, they argue about marriage too. A ברייתא teaches: if a woman married a first husband and he died, then a second and he died, she may not marry a third. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she may marry a third, but she may not marry a fourth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's second question by bringing a ברייתא. It shows that the two-or-three argument also applies to marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, two deaths make a חזקה, so she may not marry a third husband. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, it takes three deaths, so a third marriage is allowed. This shows that אביי could follow the lenient view in marriage too.

keyTerms.meaning: and it was taught in a ברייתא
the תנא who holds that three times makes a חזקה

phrases.english: Yes, and it was taught in a baraita:
If she married a first husband and he died,
a second and he died,
she may not marry a third,
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
to a third she may get married,
to a fourth she may not get married.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a ברייתא that the argument also covers marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the two-or-three argument applies only to מילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about marriage in the same way.

steps.title: Why would marriage create a pattern at all?
steps.stepSummary: With מילה, a pattern makes sense because some families have blood that does not clot well. But why would a woman's husbands keep dying?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for מילה: some families have thin blood and some have blood that clots. But for marriage, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what could make one woman's husbands die again and again. This sets up the next step, which gives two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מילה there is a clear physical reason for a pattern: bleeding runs in families. With marriage there is no obvious cause linking the husbands' deaths. So the גמרא wants to know why a חזקה would apply.

keyTerms.meaning: loose, thin blood that does not clot well

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding circumcision,
there is a family whose blood is thin
and there is a family whose blood clots,
but with marriage, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא גַּבֵּי מִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that marriage has a חזקה too, the גמרא asks for the reason behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What causes a pattern of husbands dying.

steps.title: Two causes: her body or her fortune
steps.stepSummary: One view says something in the woman's body causes the deaths (מעין גורם). רב אשי says her fortune causes them (מזל גורם).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: אבימי מהגרוניא said this in the name of רב הונא: her מעין, her body, is the cause. And רב אשי said: her מזל, her fortune, is the cause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two explanations for why a woman's husbands keep dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעין גורם points to a physical cause in the woman, tied to living with her as husband and wife. מזל גורם says it is her bad fortune, not anything physical. Step 33 shows when these two views give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: the spring causes it, a physical cause in the woman
fortune causes it, her bad luck or destiny

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi:
So said Avimi of Hagronya
in the name of Rav Huna:
The spring is the cause.
phrases.notes: "Spring" means something in her own body that harms the man who lives with her.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said: Fortune is the cause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either a physical cause in the woman (מעין) or her bad fortune (מזל).

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the מעין view and the מזל view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two explanations ever lead to a different ruling. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that a pattern of deaths counts. The question is whether the reason behind it ever changes the law in a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical outcome of the two views in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where מעין גורם and מזל גורם give different rulings.

steps.title: A husband who died before living with her, or in an accident
steps.stepSummary: The views differ when a man only did אירוסין and died, or when he died by falling from a palm tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when he betrothed her and died, or when he fell from a palm tree and died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two cases where the views lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cause is her body (מעין), a man who never lived with her, or who died in an accident, does not count toward the pattern. If the cause is her fortune (מזל), even these deaths count, since her bad luck could cause any kind of death.

keyTerms.meaning: he betrothed her (אירוסין), before living together

steps.whatToRemember: A woman whose husbands died may not remarry once there is a חזקה: two deaths for רבי, three for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Whether a death counts depends on the cause. מעין counts only deaths linked to living with her. מזל counts any death, even after אירוסין alone or in an accident.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he betrothed her and died,
or also where he fell from a palm tree and died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּאֵירְסַהּ וּמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A death after אירוסין only, or an accidental death. These count only according to the מזל view.

steps.title: רב יוסף seemed to rule both ways
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרבא tells his father רבא that רב יוסף said 'yes' when asked if the הלכה follows רבי, and also 'yes' when asked about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He asks if he was being mocked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, son of רבא, said to רבא: I asked רב יוסף, 'Is the הלכה like רבי?' and he said yes. I asked, 'Is the הלכה like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?' and he said yes. Was he laughing at me?
steps.whatsHappening: A student reports two answers from his teacher that seem to contradict each other. He asks his father רבא how both can be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree about how many times something must happen to make a pattern. רבי says two, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says three. You cannot follow both in the same case, so two 'yes' answers look like a joke.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows the view of...
Was he laughing at me? Was he mocking me?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rava, said to Rava:
I asked Rav Yosef:
phrases.notes: This רב יוסף is the great teacher, not the son who is asking. They just share a name.

phrases.english: Is the halakha like Rabbi?
And he said to me: Yes.
Is the halakha like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
And he said to me: Yes.
Was he laughing at me?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מחלוקת between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was shown, the גמרא now asks which view is the final הלכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the הלכה follow both רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל when they disagree?

steps.title: Each view is the halakha in different cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that there are unnamed משניות following each view, so the הלכה depends on the case. For marriage and lashings it follows רבי, and for a woman's monthly cycle and a goring ox it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: No. There are unnamed משניות, and he solved it for you. Marriage and lashings follow רבי. Set cycles and a forewarned ox follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that רב יוסף was not mocking. Each answer was true for a different set of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה. Some unnamed משניות follow רבי (two times is a pattern) and others follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (three times). So the count depends on the topic, not on one fixed rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Unnamed משניות, stated with no author's name
An ox known to gore, after a pattern of goring

steps.whatToRemember: Two times make a pattern for marriage and lashings, like רבי. Three times are needed for וסתות and שור המועד, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one sage 'wins' everywhere. The הלכה is split by topic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical rule for how many repeats are needed to set a חזקה in four areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him: No.
There are unnamed mishnayot, and he solved it for you:
phrases.notes: Some משניות follow each view without naming anyone, and usually the הלכה follows such an unnamed משנה.

phrases.english: Marriage and lashings follow Rabbi.
Set cycles and a forewarned ox
follow Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, סְתָמֵי הִיא וּפְשַׁיט לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רבי for marriage and lashings, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל for וסתות and שור המועד, based on unnamed משניות.

steps.title: Sources for marriage and lashings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where the marriage rule comes from (the case discussed earlier) and quotes a משנה about lashings: someone lashed twice who sins again is locked in a small chamber and fed barley until his stomach bursts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Marriage is what we said earlier. Lashings, as we learned: One who was lashed and did it again, the court puts him into a vaulted chamber and feeds him barley until his stomach bursts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving each case from step 35. Here it covers marriage and lashings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For marriage, the source is the earlier case of the woman whose husbands died. For lashings, the משנה treats a person lashed twice as having a set pattern. So on the third time he gets the harsh punishment, which fits רבי's view that two times make a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Was lashed and repeated the sin

phrases.english: Marriage: that which we said.
Lashings: as we learned in a mishna:
One who was lashed and did it again
phrases.notes: He was lashed twice, so the punishment below is for the third time he sins.

phrases.english: the court puts him into a vaulted chamber
and feeds him barley
until his stomach bursts.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִישּׂוּאִין — הָא דַּאֲמַרַן. מַלְקִיּוֹת — דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources behind the first half of רבא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי (two times) for marriage and lashings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier ברייתא about the woman, and the משנה about one who was lashed and sinned again.

steps.title: Starting the source for monthly cycles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה that shows וסתות follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The quote continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Set cycles, as we learned: A woman does not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next proof. It starts quoting the משנה about a woman's cycle, and the rest of the quote comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source for the third case in רבא's list. The full משנה, coming next, will show that a woman's cycle needs three times to be set, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman does not... (opening of the משנה)

phrases.english: Set cycles: as we learned in a mishna:
A woman does not

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָתוֹת — דִּתְנַן: אֵין הָאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources, moving to the רבן שמעון בן גמליאל side.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (three times) for וסתות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about setting a woman's cycle (quote continues in the next section).
